newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says rate cut poses no danger to A$.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says rate cut poses no danger to A$.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that the earlier announced in official cash rates posed no danger to the Australian dollar as it had been factored into the market.
Asked if he saw a danger to the Australian dollar from the rate cut, Costello told reporters: "No, I think that most of the financial markets had actually factored in this rate cut."
"It was a cut that was widely expected as a result of the very strong and good news on inflation, and I think that the financial markets have taken that in their stride," he said.
The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) earlier announced a 0.5 percentage point reduction in official cash interest rates to 5.0 percent, the fifth rate cut in a year.
The Australian dollar slipped in volatile morning trade after the RBA announcement before bouncing back.
At 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT), the local dollar was at US$0.7445/50 compared with the start on Wednesday at US$0.7455/60 and Tuesday's late US$0.7360/65.
